records.failureSummary: Implemented the scrypt password hashing unit at src/auth/passwords.mjs (new backend file). hashPassword(password) derives a 64-byte key with node:crypto scrypt (N=16384, r=8, p=1, maxmem bounded), a fresh 16-byte cryptographically random per-user salt from crypto.randomBytes, and returns a frozen record containing exactly {algorithm, salt, hash} with base64url fields and a self-describing algorithm identifier (scrypt:N=16384,r=8,p=1), so cost parameters can be raised later without invalidating stored records. serializeCredential/parseCredential provide the single-string storage form algorithm|salt|hash with strict base64url and parameter validation; verifyPassword uses crypto.timingSafeEqual, returns false (never throws) for wrong, empty, non-string or oversized passwords so a login handler can answer INVALID_CREDENTIALS, and throws a fixed-message PasswordHashError (no secret values, no cause) only for corrupt stored records. Inputs are validated at the trust boundary: password must be a UTF-8 string of 1-1024 bytes, salt 8-64 bytes, key 16-128 bytes, algorithm parameters must be a power-of-two cost within memory limits, and non-canonical base64url is rejected. The module performs no console output and stores, returns or logs no plaintext password or plaintext-derived value; its returned record is the only persistable shape. Added src/test/password-hashing.test.mjs (5 new [AC-04] node:test cases) proving with an independent node:crypto scrypt derivation that the stored hash is the real scrypt output for the stored salt, that salts differ per hash, that records contain only algorithm/salt/hash, serialization round-trips, corrupt records and tampered hashes are rejected without echoing secrets, and no console output occurs. Also added the module to the typecheck self-check's expected-exports contract in src/tools/typecheck.mjs. Verification: node --test src/test/password-hashing.test.mjs 5/5 pass; npm run lint, typecheck (8 modules) and build exit 0. The full node --test run is 30 pass / 19 fail, where all 19 failures are the pre-existing registration suites (AC-02/03/05/06/07/08 and the e2e AC-04 persistence cases) failing with HTTP 404 NOT_FOUND because POST /api/register is not implemented yet; that endpoint and the user store are outside this task's scope and none of those read-only test files were modified. No existing assertion was weakened, relaxed or deleted.
